Sandbox_Sewars.Zombies_tooltip: How many zombies are down there when a stretch of tunnel is first opened up. Shelters that were someone's last stand keep their occupants whatever this is set to.
Sandbox_Sewars.Loot_tooltip: How much is in a shelter's or hideout's crates and shelves when you first find them. Journals and sewer plans are there whatever this is set to. Only places not yet found are affected.
Sandbox_Sewars.Outfits_tooltip: Mostly ordinary: sewer workers, drifters and townsfolk; hardly any carry a bag. Mixed: some came down with a pack. Survivors: many did, and their bags are full (the mod's balance before 0.3.2). Only tunnels not yet opened up are affected.
Sandbox_Sewars.Rats_tooltip: How many of the game's own rats are down there when a stretch of tunnel is first opened up. They can be trapped, and eaten if you are hungry enough. The rodents of unusual size in the nest under Louisville are there whatever this is set to.
Sandbox_Sewars.Gas_tooltip: Some narrow culverts, well away from the ladders, hold foul air behind the county's warning placards. Breathe it without a gas mask or respirator and you get sick. Mild: queasy at worst. Harmful: sick, and it costs health while you stay. Deadly: stay and it kills. A mask with a filter keeps it out, and uses the filter up.
Sandbox_Sewars.Digging_tooltip: Whether players can widen the sewers. With a pickaxe or a sledgehammer, a square of rock can be dug out or a tunnel wall knocked through. With explosives, a bomb that goes off below ground opens the rock round it.
Sandbox_Sewars.StreetHears_tooltip: Whether zombies on one side of the street's surface come to a player on the other. No: footsteps, digging and gunfire in the sewer draw nobody on the street, a player on the street draws nobody in the sewer, and a zombie that was chasing you gives up when you climb down or out; the dead on your own level hear and see you as well as ever. Yes: the game's own rule, where a floor stops no sound, and running under a street brings its dead to stand over you.
